results.blind_working: A sugar solution has uniform composition throughout, so it is homogeneous. Sand in water is heterogeneous, and water and sodium are pure substances.
In addition, the result keeps the fewest decimal places of any term. 18.0 has one decimal place. 12.11 + 18.0 + 1.012 = 31.122, which rounds to 31.1.
Density = 25.0 g / 10.0 cm^3 = 2.50 g/cm^3. Since 1 g/cm^3 = 1000 kg/m^3, this is 2.50 x 10^3 kg/m^3.
Trailing zeros without a decimal point are not significant, so 2500 has 2 significant figures and A is false. R states this NCERT rule correctly, so R is true.

I: by the NCERT rule, when the dropped digit is 5, the preceding digit is kept if even. 4 is even, so 6.345 rounds to 6.34 and I is incorrect. II: 2.0 has two significant figures, so the product is reported as 2.5, not 2.468; II is incorrect.
Proust stated the law of definite (constant) proportions: a compound always has the same elements in the same mass ratio.
2H2 + O2 → 2H2O(g), so the volume ratio is 2:1:2. With 50 mL H2, 25 mL O2 is needed and 50 mL vapour forms.
A is true, since 2:1:2 is a simple whole-number ratio. R is false, because Gay-Lussac's law applies only to gases, not solids or liquids.

I is correct: at the same T and P, equal volumes contain equal numbers of molecules, so the volume ratio equals the mole ratio. II is incorrect: 16 g vs 32 g of O with 12 g C illustrates the law of multiple proportions, not definite proportions.
1 u is defined as 1/12 of the mass of a 12C atom, so one 12C atom has a mass of exactly 12 u. That 12 u equals about 1.99e-23 g, so option 3 is wrong. Option 4, 12 g, is the mass of one mole.
Mass = 18 × 1.66e-24 g = 2.988e-23 g, which is about 2.99e-23 g.
H2O = 18 u (III); NaCl = 58.5 u (IV); CO2 = 44 u (I); O3 = 48 u (II). This gives A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

A is correct: that is the definition of 1 u. B is correct: averages are abundance-weighted, so usually non-integral. C is false: NaCl is ionic with no discrete molecules, so 'formula mass' is the right term. D is correct: mass spectrometry gives isotopic masses and abundances. E is false: the weighted average is about 35.48 u, not the simple mean of 36.0 u. So A, B and D are correct.
1 mol H2SO4 contains 2 mol H, 1 mol S, 4 mol O and N_A molecules. So option 1 is correct.
Moles = 4.9/98 = 0.05 mol. Each molecule has 7 atoms, so 0.35 mol atoms. 0.35 x 6.022e23 = 2.108e23.
16 g O2 = 0.5 mol. Molar volume at 273.15 K and 1 bar is 22.7 L/mol, so 0.5 x 22.7 = 11.35 L.
1 mol O3 has N_A molecules, each with 3 O atoms, giving 3N_A O atoms. Both are true and R explains A.
I: 1.8 g H2O = 0.1 mol; 10 electrons per molecule gives 1 mol electrons = 6.022e23, so correct. II: 0.1 mol N2 and 0.1 mol O2 each give 0.2 mol atoms, so correct.
Molar mass of CaCO3 = 100; %O = 48/100 × 100 = 48%
A true (both have empirical formula CH). B false (composition is by mass). C true (100 - 40 - 6.7 = 53.3%). D true (24/46 = 52.17%, about 52%). E false (percentages always sum to 100%). So A, C, D.
Dividing C4H10 by the common factor 2 gives the simplest whole-number ratio C2H5.
Moles: C = 40/12 = 3.33, H = 6.67/1 = 6.67, O = 53.33/16 = 3.33, so the ratio is 1:2:1 and the empirical formula is CH2O (mass 30). Molar mass = 2 × VD = 60, so n = 2 and the formula is C2H4O2.
Moles: Fe = 70/56 = 1.25, O = 30/16 = 1.875. The ratio is 1:1.5, which is 2:3, giving Fe2O3.

Glucose (C6H12O6) and acetic acid (C2H4O2) share the empirical formula CH2O, so they have the same percentage composition; A is true. Glucose = 6 × CH2O, so R is true. R does not explain why acetic acid has the same composition; the shared empirical formula is the real reason.
Statement I is incorrect: a ratio of 1:1.33 should be multiplied by 3 to give 3:4, not rounded. Statement II is correct: M = 2 × 39 = 78, CH = 13, so n = 6 and the formula is C6H6.
C3H8 + 5O2 → 3CO2 + 4H2O. Each mole of propane gives 3 mol CO2, so 2 mol gives 6 mol CO2.
N2 = 28/28 = 1 mol; H2 = 4/2 = 2 mol. 1 mol N2 needs 3 mol H2, so H2 is limiting. NH3 formed = (2/3) × 2 = 4/3 mol; mass = (4/3) × 17 ≈ 22.67 g.
Molarity depends on solution volume, which changes with temperature. Molality, mole fraction and mass percent depend only on masses or moles.
Molarity = n/V(L) (III). Molality = n/W(kg) (I). Mole fraction of A = nA/(nA+nB) (IV). Percentage yield = actual/theoretical × 100 (II).

A: CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O, so 1 volume needs 2 volumes O2; true. B: limiting reagent is set by mole ratio, not mass; false. C: true. D: coefficients give mole or volume ratios, not mass ratios; false. E: molality is mass-based, so independent of temperature; true. Correct: A, C, E.
